newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.5 pct ahead of censure vote.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.5 pct ahead of censure vote.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose slightly in quiet and selective trade on Wednesday amid positive political expectations as Turkish parliament began debating a censure motion by the opposition to topple Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed 417.54 points, or 0.54 percent higher at 77,829.69, but down from an early high of 78,339 on profit-taking. Daily volume leapt to 16.4 trillion lira ($173 million) from Tuesday's 13.8 trillion ($146 million).
"The censure motion is expected to be rejected. Activity was share-based today without an overall rise, as was seen in the last few days," said Sarper Ozten, general manager of Oncu securities.

The index brushed a low of 77,082 in late afternoon selling prompted by the resignation of an MP from the coalition's junior conservative partner DYP ahead of the vote on the motion. But the drop was followed by selective reaction buys, brokers said.

Brokers who await support at the index's 76,000 level said the market could resume its uptrend towards 80,000 once the motion is rejected. They expect nine-month profit expectations in companies and downward t-bill yields to fuel selective demand.
The market had surged 22.7 percent from September 13 to last Wednesday's sixth consequtive all-time high close of 79,511.82 in a strong uptrend.
